defectsFoundAndCorrected.description: The credential pattern required QUOTED values. The .env / dotenv format is unquoted (KEY=value), so the check was blind to the single most likely place a real secret would ever appear. A test .env containing PROJECTONE_DB_PASSWORD=hunter2supersecret passed the check cleanly.
defectsFoundAndCorrected.impact: secret_protection is a global non-waivable invariant. A check unable to detect the obvious case protects nothing.
defectsFoundAndCorrected.correction: Added an unquoted-assignment pattern, and a rule refusing ANY committed .env file regardless of contents (only .env.example may be tracked).
defectsFoundAndCorrected.foundBy: Negative testing — deliberately writing a secret and confirming the check caught it, rather than assuming.

defectsFoundAndCorrected.description: Root-file allowlist predated the decision to use .env.example, so it rejected a file that legitimately belongs at the repository root.
defectsFoundAndCorrected.impact: Would have failed the pull request.
defectsFoundAndCorrected.correction: Allowlist extended to .env.example (and uv.lock, vite.config.ts, tsconfig.json, index.html). .env deliberately NOT added.

defectsFoundAndCorrected.description: Adding pyproject.toml activated the ruff step in CI for the first time (it had been skipped for lack of a config). 24 violations existed, most in assistant-authored governance scripts.
defectsFoundAndCorrected.impact: The pull request would have failed CI.
defectsFoundAndCorrected.correction: All violations fixed. Ruff scope narrowed to exclude the frozen framework baseline and its delivered validation/engine tooling, with reasoning recorded in pyproject.toml; governance/scripts remains linted as active project code.

defectsFoundAndCorrected.description: No line-ending normalisation existed. Windows Git converts LF to CRLF on checkout; the 87 framework baseline hashes were computed on LF content.
defectsFoundAndCorrected.impact: check_baseline_integrity.py would FAIL on the owner's machine while PASSING in CI — precisely the local/CI divergence Step 94 exists to prevent.
defectsFoundAndCorrected.correction: Added .gitattributes forcing `* text=auto eol=lf` with binary exclusions.

assistantErrorRecorded.description: The assistant ran governance checks against the OWNER'S BRANCH, found check_baseline_integrity.py absent and the workflow unfixed, and reported to the owner that a previously-claimed fix had never been deployed. That report was WRONG. The fix was in main. The owner's local clone was stale — created before the Steps 73-79 merge and never pulled — so the branch was based on a main that predated it, and inherited none of those 125 files.
assistantErrorRecorded.consequence: An unnecessary corrective bundle was issued, which then caused merge conflicts when the branch was updated. Roughly 45 minutes lost. The branch was abandoned and rebuilt from current main.
assistantErrorRecorded.rootCause: The assistant diagnosed from a derived artifact (a branch) without first comparing against the authoritative one (main). Compounding this, the assistant had been verifying against its own container copy rather than the repository — the two had silently diverged.
assistantErrorRecorded.lesson: When repository state appears wrong, compare against MAIN before concluding anything is missing. A branch is not evidence of what the repository contains. This is the same class of error as reporting a check PASS without examining the branch — asserting a conclusion from something not actually inspected.
assistantErrorRecorded.preventiveMeasure: Pull after every merge, recorded as a standing instruction. A stale local clone was the root enabler of the entire sequence.

toolingNote.finding: GitHub Desktop resolved the file-transfer problems that browser upload could not. Its Changes view shows full relative paths BEFORE committing, which is the control that would have caught the earlier flattening.
toolingNote.residualGap: Desktop separates Commit (local) from Push (remote). The owner completed a commit without pushing on two occasions, and the assistant initially misread the second as a failed push. Recorded as a standing reminder rather than a defect.
